To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
patients with NASH undergoing Roux-en-Y (RYGB) are more susceptible to transient deterioration of liver functions than after sleeve gastrectomy.
patients with NASH undergoing gastric bypass are more susceptible to deterioration of liver function tests than after gastric sleeve.

(1) RYGB induces transient increase in INR and albumine decrease at 1 month, (2) SG induces improvement in transaminase levels at 1 year, and (3) patients with NASH are more vulnerable to early liver dysfunction after RYGB than after SG.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of sleeve-gastrectomy and Roux-en-Y-gastric bypass on liver function in patients with non-alcohol fatty liver disease.
the study of the effects of bariatric surgery on liver function in patients with NA-FLD and NASH.
the study of the effects of bariatric surgery (sleeve gastrectomy and Roux-en-Y-gastric bypass) on liver function and liver histology in patients with non-alcohol related fatty liver disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RYGB is more likely than SG to cause transient deterioration in liver function in patients with NA-FLD, but that this is not clinically significant.
RYGB is associated with transient deterioration of liver functions, whereas SG induces a sustained improvement.

RYGB is associated with more significant early transient deterioration of INR and albuminaemia in NASH patients than after SG, but that SG is associated with a more significant improvement in liver function tests after 12 months in patients with NASH. (Am J Surg 2018,; 215: 1063-1072.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients with NASH should not undergo RYGB, but should undergo SG.
RYGB is associated with a transient deterioration of liver tests and INR in the first month after surgery.
patients with NASH undergoing bariatric surgery should be monitored for early changes in liver function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patients with NASH who undergo SG have significant improvement in liver function tests after 12 months.
SG and RYGB have different impacts on liver function in NASH patients.
SG and RYGB are equally efficacious in improving liver enzymes at 12 months.
